notes: White plays e4, taking central space.
Black replies with e5.
White develops the knight to f3, attacking e5.
Black defends the pawn with the knight.
White plays d4, opening the center.
Black captures on d4.
White recaptures with the knight.
Black develops the knight to f6, attacking e4.
White defends e4 by developing the knight to c3.
Black pins the c3-knight with Bb4.
White trades on c6 to damage Black's pawn structure.
Black recaptures with the b-pawn.
White develops the bishop to d3, defending e4 and aiming straight at h7.
Black strikes in the center with d5.
White captures on d5.
Black recaptures with the c-pawn, leaving a pawn on d5 that is only protected by the queen and the knight.
White castles kingside, completing development.
Black castles kingside as well.
White pins the f6-knight with Bg5, the standard plan in this structure.
Black plays the careless Re8?, which looks active but leaves the d5-pawn and the h7-square vulnerable. The correct move is 10...c6.
White captures the f6-knight with the bishop, doubling Black's pawns and removing a key defender of d5.
Black recaptures with the g-pawn, which also opens the g-file and removes the pawn shield from the g7-square.
White takes the d5-pawn with the knight, attacking Black's pieces and creating the threat of Bxh7+.
Black takes the knight with the queen, the greedy and losing reply.
White plays Bxh7+!, a deflection sacrifice that drags the king onto h7 and unmasks the queen on d1 against the black queen on d5.
Black takes the bishop with the king, since declining leaves White a whole bishop up for nothing.
White captures the black queen on d5 with Qxd5, winning a queen for a knight and a bishop.
